question: Can a knower attain final freedom even if dying in an impure place or without memory?
premises: The knower may abandon the body at a holy place or in an outcaste's house.
The knower may even have lost memory at the time of death.
One liberated simultaneously with knowledge attains absolute freedom, free from sorrow.
inference: Final liberation depends on realized knowledge, not on the purity of place or the presence of memory at death.
plain_english: Whether at a holy place or in an outcaste's house, even if memory is lost, one who abandons the body, being liberated simultaneously with knowledge, attains absolute freedom, with sorrow destroyed.
